THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 12.06.2023, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 BAIL APPL. NO. 4466 OF 2023  2  ORDER
The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.138/2023 of Valiyamala Police Station.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 498A and 306 of the IPC.

The aforesaid crime was initially registered under Section 174 of Cr.P.C. in connection with the suicide committed by the wife of the petitioner, who had allegedly consumed an overdose of certain tablets.
Subsequently, the aforesaid offences were revealed, and the same were incorporated.
2. The allegation against the petitioner is that, the victim was compelled to commit suicide because of the ill-treatment meted out by the petitioner herein by making the demand of dowry.
The petitioner was arrested in connection with the aforesaid case on 30.05.2023, and since then, he has been under judicial detention.
This application is submitted by the petitioner in such circumstances.

sentences.text: 3. Heard Sri.S.Nikhil Sankar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. C.S. Hrithwik, learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent of all the allegations.
Apart from some minor disputes between the defacto complainant and the petitioner, in connection with the day-to-day life, no serious disputes existed between them.

The learned counsel for the petitioner BAIL APPL. NO. 4466 OF 2023 also raised a contention that, the victim was having bipolar disease, and to substantiate the same Annexure 1, medical records were also relied on.

The petitioner has to look after a 12 year old boy, and if the release of the petitioner is not granted,
serious prejudice will be caused to him.

Now petitioner submits that he is ready and willing to cooperate with the investigation and shall abide by any conditions that may be imposed by this Court.
5.

On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor would oppose the aforesaid bail application by pointing out that the investigation so far conducted reveals certain materials indicating the culpability of the accused.

It is also pointed out that, on earlier occasions also, the victim submitted certain complaints of ill-treatment before the Police, as the petitioner allegedly physically assaulted the victim after consuming alcohol.

The immediate reason which persuaded the victim to commit suicide was stated as the denial of permission from the part of the petitioner to the victim to attend the marriage of a close relative, which was held on 05.02.2023.
In such circumstances, the learned Public Prosecutor would oppose the bail application.
6. I have gone through the records and heard the contentions raised from both sides.
There are indeed allegations against the petitioner.

However, considering the nature of the allegations and gravity thereof, and also taking note of the period of detention that the petitioner had already undergone, I am BAIL APPL. NO. 4466 OF 2023 of the view that the petitioner can be granted bail.
While taking this view I have considered the contention of the petitioner that the victim has bi-polar disease , as revealed from Annexure 1.
There is substantial progress in the investigation as well.
Therefore the petitioner can be granted bail by incorporating appropriate conditions to ensure his continued cooperation with the investigation.

Accordingly, this application is allowed, and the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on the following conditions:
i) The petitioner shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
ii) The petitioner shall fully cooperate with the investigation.
iii) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m on every Wednesday until the filing of the final report.
iv) The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.

Nizam N vs State Of Kerala on 12 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132030141/
2 v) The petitioner shall not commit any offence of similar nature while on bail.
vi) The petitioner shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way BAIL APPL. NO. 4466 OF 2023 try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
vii) The petitioner shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the jurisdictional court.
viii) The petitioner shall surrender his passport before the Jurisdictional court, and, in case he does not have a passport, an affidavit to that effect shall be filed.
